title: One alternative to one hard-to-reverse decision
description: IDE-69 §4.3. One provider call produces exactly one alternative, so this schema types one alternative and not a round: a call that is forbidden from returning more than one cannot satisfy a whole-round schema. The script issues the two or three calls, collects the validated documents and builds the comparison table itself — the table is rendering, and rendering belongs to the script. There is no recommendation field here: at сведение the architect recommends, and `when_it_wins`/`when_it_loses` are the material they recommend from. Written for strict structured output: every object lists every one of its properties in `required` and forbids additional ones, and the one optional field is optional by being nullable rather than by being absent (IDE-103).

decision_id.description: The id of the hard-to-reverse decision in the ADR's decision registry that this is an alternative to. Alternatives are generated per decision, never per document: one alternative spread over a whole ADR compares nothing.

name.description: A short name for the alternative, distinct from the decision it competes with. A name that paraphrases the decision is the first sign of a pass that converged.

sketch.description: How it would actually be built: modules, interfaces, the seam it puts the boundary at.

axes.description: The five fixed comparison axes from IDE-69 §4.3. Fixed because a table with free columns is prose in table markup — and free columns are impossible here by construction, since these five keys are the only ones this object accepts.

depth.description: How much behaviour sits behind one unit of interface.

locality.description: Where a change under this alternative lands.

seam_placement.description: Where the boundary is drawn, and what is on each side of it.

testability.description: What can be tested without the rest of the system, and what cannot.

cost_of_reversal.description: What undoing this would cost: a migration, a coordinated change in two repositories, or an afternoon.

when_it_wins.description: The conditions under which this alternative is the better choice.

when_it_loses.description: The conditions under which it is the worse choice. An alternative that only wins is an advertisement, not an alternative.

addresses_practice_finding.description: Names the external practice finding this alternative takes up, when best practice contradicted the decision. Null when there was no such finding. IDE-69 §4.2 obliges the alternative pass to consider a contradicting approach, and this field is how that obligation becomes mechanical: for a flagged decision the script refuses a round in which no alternative fills it in.
